scenario: A 34-year-old patient has a positive skin test after household exposure. The film is normal. He has no cough, no fever, and no night sweats. A classmate orders four drugs because the skin test is positive. He feels well. He cannot produce sputum.
question: Why are four drugs the wrong regimen?
options: A normal film and no symptoms mean the positive skin test is not active disease
A positive skin test with a normal film is active disease
Inability to produce sputum means four drugs are required
Feeling well means the skin test is false and still needs four drugs
No night sweats means four drugs are the smaller regimen
correctAnswer: A normal film and no symptoms mean the positive skin test is not active disease
explanation: Four drugs are the wrong regimen, because the film is normal and he has no cough, fever, or night sweats. A normal film and no symptoms mean the positive skin test is not active disease. A positive skin test with a normal film is active disease is not. Inability to produce sputum means four drugs are required means there is no sputum suggesting active disease. Feeling well means the skin test is false and still needs four drugs is a real latent infection. No night sweats means four drugs are the smaller regimen is why fewer drugs fit.
